Specification for bayesnec support in toxval

Source: BAYESNEC-claude.md

The implementation specification for toxval_predict() methods for fits made with bayesnec: function signatures, the calls each method makes, invariants, edge cases, the measurements behind each decision, and the alternatives rejected.

BAYESNEC-human.md is the plan. Read it first. Section numbers are the same in both documents. Each decision is stated in full here and once only.

Facts about bayesnec are cited as file:line on origin/predev at 116ea91b (2026-10-20, version 2.1.3.42) unless marked [master], which is the CRAN release 2.1.3.1 at 6f6bd25d. toxval facts are cited on phase-7-bayesnec-methods at 6bdd99c, the head of PR #66. Measurements were run on 2026-10-23 in R 4.6.1 under WSL with bayesnec 2.1.3.39 installed.

T35 was written into notes/implementation/02_decisions.md on 2026-10-29 (task 0).

1. The decision (T35)

toxval contains the toxval_predict() methods for bayesnec fits. Agreed by RF and AP on 2026-10-23, and proposed in #68.

1.1 Reason

A toxval_pred holds facts that toxval defines for its own compute functions and that bayesnec has no use for: the keys table (T14), meta$x_control (T21), the per-realisation asymptotes (T24), the per-curve trials (T26), and, for a model-averaged fit, the equation behind each realisation (§3.2). Each of these was added or changed during phases 2 to 4. Had the methods been in bayesnec, each change would have needed a bayesnec release made after the toxval release that introduced it, and bayesnec could not import toxval at all until toxval was on CRAN (#45).

1.2 Passages the decision overrides

Each passage below states or depends on the earlier split, in which bayesnec held the methods and imported toxval. Task 0 edits them.

1.3 Parts of the earlier plan that stand

toxval_pred stays exported and documented, and changes to its contract stay breaking changes. Another package may still supply a toxval_predict() method, and #21 (glm, gam) uses the same seam. Only the reason given for it in §3.3 of the refactor plan changes.

1.4 Rejected alternative

The methods in bayesnec, as #39 proposed. Rejected for the reason in §1.1: every toxval_pred contract change becomes a two-package release, and support for bayesnec fits waits on CRAN publication of toxval.

2. User-visible behaviour

2.1 The predictor scale

toxval reports estimates on the scale of the variable named inside crf(). For crf(log(x), ...) that is x. bayesnec::ecx() and bayesnec::nsec() report the same fit on the log(x) scale.

The mechanism:

  • bayesnec takes the predictor as all.vars() of the first argument of crf() (bayesnecformula.R:821-826), so bnec_pop["x_var"] is "x".
  • The transformed term is substituted into the brms nonlinear formula (bayesnecformula.R:843-845, :868-872), so Stan applies log() and the brmsfit data hold raw x.
  • prediction_grid() builds the grid over raw x (expand_classes.R:319-326; the comment at helpers.R:2380-2386).
  • bayesnec finds the crossing on that grid, then applies the crf() transformation to the estimate with sub_x_transformation() (helpers.R:2409-2430, called at ecx.R:267 and nsec.R:310), and prints a once-per-call message (ecx.R:84-88). Reporting on the recorded scale by default is decided for bayesnec 3.0 as D41 (03_decisions.md:568) and not implemented.

toxval takes x_vec from the same grid column and applies no transformation, so its estimates are on the raw scale. xform is applied afterwards (T6), so a user who supplies xform = exp for an inline log() gets exp(x). The method documentation says so. A predictor transformed into its own column before fitting, such as x = log(concentration) in the data, is unaffected: the grid is then over that column.

Test (task 5, tests/local/): on the crf(log(x)) fixture, each toxval ECx realisation equals exp() of the matching bayesnec::ecx(posterior = TRUE) realisation.

2.2 Differences from bayesnec’s numbers

quantity toxval bayesnec source
nsec reference, model-averaged fit each equation’s control by default (anchor = "component", T12) each equation’s own control T12
realisation with no crossing placed by amended T21 corresponding NSEC rule, with a bound when censored T21, D17 amendment
directions both, as rows (T10) decreasing —
default resolution 500 (T31) 500 for post-fit endpoints T31
control first grid value, x_control, the lowest observed x unless x_control is supplied (T41) prediction at the lowest observed x helpers.R:2697-2742
interpolation linear between grid points linear helpers.R:2483-2507

The last two rows agree, so under type = "absolute", at equal resolution and with x_range and x_control unset, the decreasing ECx of every realisation that crosses within the grid should equal bayesnec’s up to the accuracy of bayesnec’s root-finding. toxval interpolates the crossing exactly. bayesnec’s crossing_x() instead finds the root of the same piecewise-linear interpolant with modelbased’s .uniroot.all(), at a tolerance of .Machine$double.eps^0.2 in grid steps. On bayesnec_nec4param at resolution = 200 (2026-10-29, bayesnec 2.1.3.43), the interpolant at toxval’s crossing differed from the reference by at most 8.9e-16, and at bayesnec’s by up to 2.8e-6. The two crossings differed by at most 3.2e-7 relative. Task 5 therefore tests that they agree to that tolerance times the grid step. A larger discrepancy means that one of the packages locates the crossing incorrectly.

T21 as amended on #74 (RF, 2026-10-27) now also applies in bayesnec. A draw past the reference at control with no later decreasing crossing is censored above the range when its first meaningful response change is an increase and it later lies on the no-effect side. A later decreasing crossing is returned. Historical comparisons to the old control rule are recorded in T21. Realisations that cross are unaffected, so the task 5 comparison stands.

3. Design

3.1 Sources of the grid and the curves

Signature

toxval_predict.bayesnecfit <- function(
  object,
  ...,
  x_var = NULL,
  group_var = NULL,
  resolution = 500,
  x_range = NULL,
  x_control = NULL
)

resolution follows the generic’s default of 500 (T31, 6bdd99c). ... follows object and an unused argument is an error (T39). x_control is the argument #73 adds (T41).

Body

check_bayesnec_installed()
chk_bayesnec_supported(object)
chk_no_group_var(group_var, "`bayesnecfit`")
x_var <- bnec_x_var(object$bayesnecformula, object$fit$data, x_var)
newdata <- bnec_grid(
  object,
  predict_grid(x_range, object$fit$data[[x_var]], resolution, x_control)
)
x_vec <- newdata[[x_var]]
curve <- posterior_epred(object$fit, newdata = newdata, re_formula = NA)
chk_defined_grid(list(curve), x_vec)

new_toxval_pred(
  curves = list(curve),
  keys = group_keys(),
  x_vec = x_vec,
  meta = build_meta(
    object = object,
    x_vec = x_vec,
    x_var = x_var,
    curves = list(curve),
    realisation = "draws",
    family = object$fit$family$family
  )
)

Helpers

check_bayesnec_installed() stops with “bayesnec must be installed to compute on a <class>.” when requireNamespace("bayesnec", quietly = TRUE) is FALSE. The requireNamespace() call is in its own one-line function, bayesnec_available(), so that a test can replace it with testthat::local_mocked_bindings().

bnec_x_var(formula, data, x_var):

found <- attr(stats::model.frame(formula, data = data), "bnec_pop")[["x_var"]]

stats::model.frame() dispatches to bayesnec’s registered method model.frame.bayesnecformula (bayesnecformula.R:748-759), which is also in the CRAN release [master NAMESPACE]. This is how newdata_eval() found the predictor before phase 3 (58c57a1^:R/helpers.R:23). Rules:

  • length(found) != 1 stops: the crf() term names more than one variable. bayesnec refuses the same case when it back-transforms (sub_x_transformation(), helpers.R:2409-2430).
  • x_var = NULL takes found.
  • A supplied x_var that differs from found stops, naming both, as T17 does for a drc fit.

bnec_grid(object, x_vec):

bayesnec::bnec_newdata(
  object,
  resolution = length(x_vec),
  x_range = range(x_vec)
)

predict_grid() chooses the concentrations, so the refusals and warnings of T41 apply to a bnec() fit as to a brmsfit. bnec_newdata() builds its grid with seq(min(x_range), max(x_range), length = resolution) (prediction_grid()), as predict_grid() does, so its predictor column is identical to x_vec.

bnec_newdata() is exported in both the CRAN and the development release. It sets the trials column to 1 for binomial and beta_binomial (expand_classes.R:327-330) and a rate() denominator to 1 (expand_classes.R:331-345), and adds level columns only for a joint refit, which is out of scope (§3.3). It builds no response column and no group-level variables, so group-level effects must be marginalised: re_formula = NA, as every bayesnec curve prediction does (expand_classes.R:281-291) and as T16 specifies for brmsfit.

build_meta() takes x_control from x_vec[1] (T41), so it needs no access to the data of a bnecfit, which are object$fit$data rather than object$data. It gains ..., a set of optional elements appended to the list (§3.4). The brmsfit and drc methods pass none and are unchanged.

By default x_control is then the lowest observed predictor value, which is what bayesnec reads its control at (control_x(), helpers.R:2554-2572).

Refusals

chk_bayesnec_supported(object) stops, naming the class or family, when:

  • inherits(object, "bayesnecjointlevel"). The class is internal to bayesnec (bayesnecjointfit-methods.R:24-44) and inherits bayesnecfit, so dispatch would reach this method with a grid over every level’s data.
  • object$fit$family$family is one of hurdle_gamma, hurdle_poisson, hurdle_negbinomial or zero_inflated_beta. bayesnec fits these with a second block for the zeros, named hu or zi (data-raw/sysdata.R:73-74, hurdle_family.R:21-36). Their default expected value is the combined mean, and bayesnec reports either block through dpar (hurdle_family.R:221-244). Which to report is the decision deferred to the hurdle pull request (§3.3).
  • isTRUE(attr(object$bayesnecformula, "bayesnec_internal_truncation")) with a poisson or negbinomial family (hurdle_family.R:154-157). For this formula brms returns a truncated expectation summed over a finite grid, and bayesnec replaces it with the closed form (hurdle_family.R:171-207). It arises only as the growth component of bnec_hurdle() (bnec_hurdle.R:275-288), which a user can extract as hurdle_fit$growth.
  • group_var is not NULL. A bnec() fit has one curve: its group-level terms (ogl(), pgl(), (par | g)) are marginalised, as under T16.

toxval_predict.bnecfit() is the method for every other bnecfit subclass. It stops naming class(object)[1] and the two supported classes. The bayesnecfit and bayesmanecfit methods are more specific and dispatch first.

Measurement

On the nec4param component of manec_example, over a 50-point bnec_newdata() grid, brms::posterior_epred(<component>$fit, newdata, re_formula = NA) and bayesnec’s posterior_epred() on the pulled-out bayesnecfit gave identical 100 × 50 matrices (all.equal(tolerance = 0)).

Calling brms::posterior_epred() on a bnecfit object itself, rather than on $fit, fails with “no applicable method” unless the bayesnec namespace is loaded, and dispatches to bayesnec’s method once it is.

Rejected alternatives

  • Curves from bayesnec‘s own posterior_epred() methods. They give the same matrices for the classes in scope, but there is no method for the prebayesnecfit components of a model set, and posterior_epred.bayesmanecfit() binds the equations’ rows without saying which rows came from which equation (posterior_epred.R:66-77). One call on the brmsfit serves both classes.
  • No use of bayesnec at all. The predictor would have to be found by parsing the formula, which bayesnec does by evaluating the term with its internal crf() (bayesnecformula.R:786-788, :1709-1726), and the trials and rate rules of the grid would have to be copied. Both have changed recently in bayesnec (#136 for the rate, #382 for level terms).
  • bayesnec::pull_brmsfit() in place of object$fit. It returns object$fit for a bayesnecfit (pull_brmsfit.R:30-32) and has no method for a prebayesnecfit, so the field is read directly in both methods.

3.2 Model-averaged fits

Structure

A bayesmanecfit holds mod_fits, a named list of prebayesnecfit objects, each list(fit, model, init, bayesnecformula) (fit_bayesnec.R:183-185), and mod_stats, a data frame whose wi column holds the model weights with rows named by equation (expand_classes.R:517-522; row names confirmed on manec_example). Weights are pseudo-BMA by default (helpers.R:1302-1304). Since 2.1.3.7 the object also holds w_draw_seed and w_draw_index (expand_classes.R:537-539, :579); earlier objects do not (bayesmanecfit-class.R:41-44), and the CRAN release has neither.

The average in bayesnec

posterior_epred.bayesmanecfit() (posterior_epred.R:66-77):

  1. predicts each equation;
  2. takes n, the smallest number of draws among the equations;
  3. keeps, for each equation m, the rows w_draw_index[[m]];
  4. binds them in the order of names(mod_fits).

pull_draw_index() (helpers.R:215-227) uses the stored index when object$sample_size == n and every equation is named in it. Otherwise weighted_draw_index() (helpers.R:180-196) rebuilds it:

set.seed(seed, sample.kind = "Rejection")  # seed is w_draw_seed, or 216
lapply(model_set, function(m) sample(seq_len(n), as.integer(round(n * wi[[m]]))))

inside a function that restores the caller’s random number state. Each equation contributes round(n * wi) draws, sampled without replacement. The total can differ from n by rounding. The CRAN release used an unseeded sample() on every call [master helpers.R:84-87, 102-106].

Specification

toxval_predict.bayesmanecfit() has the signature of §3.1. Its body:

  1. The checks of §3.1, applied to each component’s family and formula.
  2. model_set <- names(object$mod_fits) and wi <- object$mod_stats[model_set, "wi"].
  3. One family across the set, or stop. bnec() fits a set with one family, so a failure here means a malformed object.
  4. x_var from the first component, as bnec_x_var(mod_fits[[1]]$bayesnecformula, mod_fits[[1]]$fit$data, x_var).
  5. The grid from bnec_grid(object, ...).
  6. For each equation, posterior_epred(mod_fits[[m]]$fit, newdata, re_formula = NA).
  7. n <- min(nrow(...)) over the equations.
  8. The index from bnec_draw_index(object, model_set, wi, n), which reproduces pull_draw_index(): the stored w_draw_index under the same three conditions, and otherwise the rebuild above, with the seed taken from object$w_draw_seed or 216. The rebuild runs inside withr::with_preserve_seed(), so the caller’s .Random.seed and RNGkind() are unchanged.
  9. The curve matrix is the equations’ rows at the index, bound in model_set order, and is passed to chk_defined_grid() as in §3.1. meta$draw_model is rep(model_set, lengths(index)).
  10. meta$model_weights is stats::setNames(wi, model_set), and meta$seed is the seed the index was built from.

An equation whose round(n * wi) is 0 contributes no realisation. It is absent from draw_model and listed in model_weights.

Measurement

On manec_example (bayesnec 2.1.3.39, which holds no w_draw_index or w_draw_seed), a 50-point grid, and the rebuild with seed 216, the matrix built by steps 2 to 9 was identical to bayesnec::posterior_epred(manec_example, newdata) (all.equal(tolerance = 0)): 100 realisations, 83 from nec4param and 17 from ecx4param.

bnec_newdata() on a bayesmanecfit calls pull_out() on the first equation (bnec_newdata.R:63-68), which recomputes that equation’s summaries. With a 500-point grid it took 1.12 s on manec_example, against 0.007 s on a bayesnecfit. Since only the first equation is pulled out, its run time is set by that equation’s draws rather than by the number of equations, so a set of two equations measures it.

Task 3 measured it on a set of nec4param and ecx4param fitted to nec_data with four chains of 1000 retained draws, 4000 per equation (seed = 4000, bayesnec 2.1.3.39). The 30 s at which the task was to stop was not approached:

resolution bnec_newdata() posterior_epred(), both equations
200 3.0 s 0.7 s
500 3.2 s 0.9 s
1000 4.9 s 1.6 s

toxval_predict() at the default 500 took 5.8 s, and ecx() 3.7 s on a second call. The fit held a w_draw_index (seed 815105072, weights 0.846 and 0.154), so the stored index was used, giving 3385 and 615 realisations. The matrix was identical to bayesnec::posterior_epred() over the same grid.

The choice of index

An index drawn by toxval from a seed argument, as toxval_predict.drc() draws its bootstrap, was rejected. It would give a second model-averaged posterior of the same object, so a bayesnec plot and a toxval estimate would describe different draws. bayesnec has already made its index reproducible without a user seed (#216); reproducing it takes about ten lines and one comparison test. The risk is that bayesnec changes its rule. The comparison test in task 3 fails if it does.

The component anchor

anchor = "component" (T23, REFACTOR-claude.md §3.8) takes each equation’s reference from the control of every draw of that equation’s fit, including the draws left out of the average:

reference[m] <- quantile(model_control[[i]][[m]], sig_val)

applied to that equation’s realisations, with ecnsec paired to it. toxval_predict.bayesmanecfit() predicts every draw of every equation before keeping the rows of the index, so meta$model_control is the first column of each equation’s prediction (§3.4) and needs no further prediction. Where a toxval_pred has meta$draw_model but no meta$model_control, as one built by another method might, component_reference() takes each equation’s quantile over its realisations. Without meta$draw_model, every realisation belongs to one equation and "component" equals "model", which is T23’s statement for every other class.

compute_nsec() then holds reference as one value per realisation, a list column as compute_ecx() already gives, and summarise_metric() reports its prob_vals[1] quantile, as it does for control. On manec_example that is the nec4param reference, which holds 83 of the 100 realisations. Reporting one reference per equation would need a column whose length varies with the model set.

bayesnec::nsec() on a model set computes each equation’s NSEC from that equation’s full posterior and then keeps the rows of the index (nsec.R:425-456; the per-equation reference at :422-424), so the two packages take the same references. On manec_example, in one deterministic run at resolution = 200 and sig_val = 0.01 with bayesnec 2.1.3.43 (2026-10-29), the decreasing NSEC was 1.47399 (0.76562, 1.55067) from both. The NSEC of each realisation agreed to within bayesnec’s root-finding tolerance (§2.2), and the realisations past their reference at the control were the same in both. tests/local/test-bayesnec-compare.R asserts both.

The reference over the realisations alone (rejected)

Taking each equation’s reference over its realisations in the average, quantile(control[draw_model == m], sig_val), was implemented first. RF accepted the resulting difference from bayesnec on 2026-10-23 and reversed that on 2026-10-29, once it was measured. Its reference for ecx4param on manec_example is a quantile of 17 control draws, against bayesnec’s 100. Both estimate the same quantile, so the 83 ecx4param draws left out add information and nothing is gained by leaving them out. The rejection of storing the full control, that it would only reproduce bayesnec to within Monte Carlo error, assumed the difference was noise.

Measured in the same run, the decreasing NSEC was 1.4741 (0.5900, 1.5508) under this rule, against 1.4740 (0.7656, 1.5507) from bayesnec::nsec(). The estimate and the upper limit agree to about 1e-4, and the lower limit is 0.176 lower.

The ecx4param reference accounts for the lower limit. The type-7 1% quantile of 17 values lies 0.16 of the way from the lowest to the second lowest. The 17 realisations kept in the average exclude the two lowest of the equation’s 100 control draws, so the reference was 2.139 in toxval and 2.097 in bayesnec. Five of the 100 controls lie below the first and one below the second. The 16 ecx4param realisations that cross within the grid cross toxval’s reference 0.053 to 0.197 lower. The 17th, realisation 97, has a control of 2.131. It is past toxval’s reference at the control and crosses bayesnec’s at 0.385.

The 2.5% limit of 100 realisations lies 0.475 of the way from the third lowest to the fourth. In both packages these are realisations 87 and 88, at 0.571 and 0.611 in toxval and at 0.728 and 0.808 in bayesnec. The two below them are realisation 6, a nec4param draw past its reference at the control in both, and realisation 97. Where realisation 97 is placed therefore does not change the limit. The nec4param reference is 2.0345 in toxval and 2.0352 in bayesnec, which accounts for the differences of about 1e-4 in the estimate and the upper limit.

The size of the shift depends on the number of realisations of an equation. For a continuous distribution, E[F(X₍ₖ₎)] = k / (n + 1), so the type-7 quantile at p of n values has on average about h / (n + 1) of the distribution below it, where h = 1 + p(n − 1). At p = 0.01 that is 0.064 for n = 17, 0.020 for n = 100, 0.012 for n = 615 (the ecx4param realisations of the task 3 set) and 0.010 for n = 3385. A reference taken from few realisations therefore lies nearer the centre of the equation’s control distribution on average, and that equation’s NSECs are lower in both directions. manec_example holds 100 draws per equation. On a fit of 4000 draws per equation, an equation of weight 0.01 contributes 40 realisations, whose 1% quantile has on average 0.034 of the distribution below it.

3.3 Classes

class [master] structure first PR needs
bayesnecfit yes fit, model, bayesnecformula, summaries (expand_classes.R:243-252) yes —
bayesmanecfit yes mod_fits, mod_stats, sample_size, index (expand_classes.R:577-584) yes —
bayesnecfit, two-block family — hurdle element (expand_classes.R:172-221) no dpar
bayesnechurdlefit no growth, survival fits (bnec_hurdle.R:342-344) no which
bayesnecgroupfit no one fit per level in fits (bnec_group.R:478-485) no per-curve grid
bayesnecjointfit no one brmsfit over levels (bnec_joint.R:436-444) no per-curve grid

Class vectors: bnec.R:1096, :1102, :1123; bnec_hurdle.R:345; bnec_group.R:486; bnec_joint.R:445.

The combined curve of a hurdle pair is the product of the growth and survival curves, paired by row after both are cut to the smaller number of draws (bayesnechurdlefit-class.R:63-101), over the survival fit’s range. bayesnec selects with which = "combined" | "growth" | "survival" and refuses type = "relative" (:309-318). A toxval method needs which and a ruling on relative.

In a group fit each level is an independent bnec() fit to that level’s rows (bnec_group.R:379-382, :424-426), with its own concentrations and possibly its own number of draws. Rows of different levels are different, unrelated draws.

A joint refit is one brmsfit with the level in the population-level part of every curve parameter, so its draws are aligned across levels. Since D40 (ce670a39) each level is read over its own concentrations (bayesnecjointfit-methods.R:66-81, :291-302). bayesnec’s control_posterior() has no branch for a level and reads the control at the lowest concentration across all levels (helpers.R:2723-2742), which disagrees with the level’s own search start (nsec.R:298-300) when levels do not share it.

Both of the last two conflict with the toxval_pred contract: one x_vec checked against every curve (chk_curves(), R/toxval-pred.R:373-403), one meta$x_control, and one meta$n_realisation. Supporting them needs a ruling on whether x_vec and x_control become per curve. That is a breaking change to a public contract, so it is decided on its own pull request, not here.

3.4 Additions to toxval_pred

Optional metadata

element type rule
meta$draw_model character, length n_realisation no NA; every value in names(meta$model_weights) when that is present
meta$model_weights named numeric names unique and non-empty; values in [0, 1]; sum equal to 1 by all.equal()
meta$model_control unnamed list, one element per row of keys, of named lists of numeric vectors requires meta$draw_model; every model in draw_model named; each vector numeric, of any length

draw_model and model_weights are checked in chk_meta() when not NULL. model_control is checked in chk_model_control(), called from validate_toxval_pred() because its length is checked against keys. It has one element per curve, as control and asymptote do, because the control is a property of the curve. Each vector holds every draw of the equation’s own fit, so its length is that fit’s number of draws, not n_realisation. All three are documented in the Metadata section of ?new_toxval_pred as optional. The change is additive: every existing object stays valid. meta$seed is documented as the seed of a bootstrap or of a model-averaging index.

How the result reports model_weights, which REFACTOR-claude.md §3.10 requires for a relative estimate that drops equations, is decided with the phase 4 implementation of relative. The toxval tibble keeps meta[settings_required()] only (R/toxval-tbl.R:18-22).

The asymptote slot (after T24)

Per realisation, from the equation that produced it:

  • decreasing: the b_bot_Intercept draw where "b_bot_Intercept" %in% brms::variables(fit) (parameter names curve_params.R:536-543, used as such at ecx.R:510); 0 where the equation has no bot and the family is bounded below; NA where it has none and the family is gaussian or student, the two with no lower bound in bayesnec’s own test (helpers.R:2694);
  • increasing: response_upper_bound(), which is 1 for a proportion and NA otherwise. No bayesnec equation has an upper-asymptote parameter: top is the response at zero concentration of a decreasing curve.

The equations with bot are found from the draws rather than from a list. The result matches the nine named in REFACTOR-claude.md §3.10 and mod_groups$bot_free (data-raw/sysdata.R:20-23). Under a link other than identity bot is on the link scale (hurdle_family.R:45-49). bnec() uses the identity link unless the user wrote one (bayesnecformula.R:253-257), so a non-identity link sets the asymptote to NA and relative then refuses the fit, as §3.10 specifies for an undefined asymptote.

On a model set the slot is filled from each equation’s rows at the index, so alignment holds by construction. Dropping the equations whose asymptote is NA and renormalising, as §3.10 specifies, is equivalent to excluding their realisations; the warning of T25 then gives the excluded fraction. §3.10 also asks for the equations to be named. Under relative, compute_ecx() and compute_nsec() warn with the names of the equations whose asymptote is NA in a direction where another equation has one. A direction with no asymptote in any equation is excluded for every realisation, and T25’s warning reports it, as for a single fit.

The response bound

A bnec() fit is predicted with one trial (expand_classes.R:327-330), so its binomial or beta_binomial curve is a proportion and the bound is 1. Task 2 implemented this as a branch on source_class in response_upper_bound() (R/compute.R), because a brms binomial fit was then bounded at NA. T26, amended on PR #66 (2436858), predicts a brms binomial fit at one trial and bounds every binomial family at 1, so the branch was removed (c3c0dd8).

The threshold slot

Left NULL. A NEC is b_nec_Intercept (expand_classes.R:147) and exists only for the ten NEC equations (data-raw/sysdata.R:6-8). In a model set it would be NA for the realisations of the others, and what such a realisation contributes to an N(S)EC is the question #25 is open for. Filling the slot before #25 rules would fix that meaning by default.

3.5 bayesnec behaviour not reproduced

  • The back-transformation by the crf() term (§2.1; T6).
  • The refusal of an absolute ECx for a gaussian fit of an equation without bot. bayesnec removed it, following OECD TG 201, with a comment at ecx.R:234-237, which agrees with REFACTOR-claude.md §3.10. The guard in §3.7 of the refactor plan, and the second of the “two guards needing homes” on #39, are deleted.
  • Per-equation computation then mixing (ecx.R:398-428, nsec.R:425-456). Every metric is computed on the averaged matrix (§3.2).
  • The decline from the peak, hormesis_def = "max", which defines a different reference and is not reimplemented (T28; further references are the scope of #63). bayesnec 2.1.3.43 no longer takes the argument.

3.6 The shared function names

bayesnec exports ecx(), nsec(), nec() and ecnsec(). Its methods (NAMESPACE, checked 2026-10-23):

  • origin/predev: ecx for bayesnecfit, bayesmanecfit, bayesnecgroupfit, bayesnechurdlefit, bayesnecjointfit; nsec for the same five plus brmsfit and drc;
  • [master]: ecx and nsec for bayesnecfit and bayesmanecfit, and nsec for brmsfit and drc.

After phase 4 toxval::ecx() and toxval::nsec() are plain functions calling toxval_predict() (REFACTOR-claude.md §3.3). With both packages attached the later one masks the earlier. With bayesnec attached last, ecx(<brmsfit>) stops with “no applicable method” and nsec(<brmsfit>) runs bayesnec’s copy, the hazard #39 measured on 2026-08-19.

This work adds a paragraph to the README and to ?ecx and ?nsec advising toxval::ecx(). An .onAttach() message was rejected. It would print for every user who attaches both packages and would not change which function runs.

The remedy is in bayesnec: keep, rename or retire its functions, or call toxval’s. That is not decided here.

3.7 Robustness across bayesnec structures

After task 3, both methods were run on one fit of every structure a user can build on bayesnec predev at 116ea91b (2.1.3.42), and on the five structures that CR_workflows fits. Two read-only surveys listed the structures: one of the bayesnec source and one of CR_workflows, whose only bnec() call is pkg/R/fit_bayesnec.R:85. bayesnec was loaded from an export of 116ea91b with pkgload::load_all(), without installing it.

Each fit was predicted at resolution = 50. The curve matrix was compared with identical() against bayesnec’s own method: brms::posterior_epred(<fit>, newdata = bnec_newdata(fit, 50), re_formula = NA). re_formula = NA is passed because bayesnec’s posterior_epred() methods set neither newdata nor re_formula, while its own curve predictions in expand_nec() use re_formula = NA. Every equation of a model set was also pulled out with pull_out() and compared as a bayesnecfit, as were the per-level fits of a group fit and the two parts of a hurdle pair. ecx(), and summarise_metric(compute_nsec()), were then run on each prediction. Fits used two chains of 500 retained draws unless stated otherwise. The CR_workflows sets were refitted with that repository’s formulas, identity-link families and simulated datasets (pkg/data/*.rda), with the same short sampler.

structure fits
families gaussian, beta, gamma, binomial and beta_binomial with trials(), poisson, poisson with rate(), negbinomial, bernoulli, zero_inflated_poisson
formula terms crf(log(x)), crf(sqrt(x)), weights(), cens(), pgl(g) on beta, ogl(g) on beta and on gaussian, (top \| g) on gamma, disp(~x), disp("power"), log(y) as response, beta with a logit link
model sets every equation on nec_data (17 kept); amend(drop = ) to three; + of two fits; four chains with thin = 3
CR_workflows decline sets on gamma, binomial, negbinomial and beta, and an all set on gamma, each with a control at concentration 0
classes the per-level fits of a bnec_group() fit; the gamma growth and Bernoulli survival parts of a bnec_hurdle() fit

The results:

  • All 128 predicted objects, 33 fits and 95 components, were identical to bayesnec’s matrix. The predicted objects comprise the 24 single fits, the 9 model sets, the 89 equations pulled out of those sets, the 4 group levels and the 2 hurdle parts.
  • ecx() and the NSEC computation ran without error on every one.
  • The refusals gave their messages on real objects. The objects were a hurdle_gamma fit, a bayesnecgroupfit, a bayesnechurdlefit, a bayesnecjointfit, and a bayesnecjointlevel built with bayesnec:::joint_level_fit().
  • With thin = 3, four chains and 500 post-warmup iterations, each equation held 668 draws while sample_size recorded 667. At the time of this measurement, toxval bypassed the stored index and rebuilt 668 realisations, while bayesnec kept the stored index of 667 draws. Toxval now recognises this legacy undercount and uses the same stored count and index as bayesnec (#477). bayesnec_manec_example holds 100 draws per equation and records 100, so the task 5 comparison on it is unaffected. The decline sets on binomial and beta gave 1001 and 999 realisations, from rounding each equation’s share. Both packages do the same.
  • In a session using RNGkind("L'Ecuyer-CMRG"), the rebuilt index again matched bayesnec. It differed from the index rebuilt under the default generator, because weighted_draw_index() fixes the seed and the sample kind but not the generator.

zero_inflated_poisson and zero_inflated_negbinomial are accepted. bayesnec leaves them out of its two-part registry (data-raw/sysdata.R:60-74): brms fits them as a mixture with a constant zero-inflation probability, so their expected value is one curve.

Four structures could not be fitted, and so are not covered:

  • the zero-truncated count part of bnec_hurdle(), which needs brms 2.23.2 (2.23.0 is installed), so its refusal is tested on an altered copy only;
  • disp(~z) with a covariate other than x, for which bnec() itself fails after sampling (bayesnec #443);
  • + on fits with different numbers of draws, which bayesnec refuses (“Each object in the list must have the same dimensions”);
  • pull_out() with two equations, which 2.1.3.42 refuses (“Argument model can only take one value”).

One case gives a wrong upper bound, found from the code rather than from a fit. With a trials() expression rather than a column, such as trials(n * 2), bnec_newdata() sets n to 1 and the curve is predicted for two trials. response_upper_bound() then gives 1 for a curve that reaches 2. A bare trials() column, the form in every example found, is unaffected.

The scripts are in tests/local/bayesnec-robustness/, and its README.md gives their order and settings. compare-fits.R makes the comparison and check-edges.R the checks on the joint level, the log predictor, the thinned set and the generator. The fits are written to the user cache rather than the repository, because they take about 3.3 GB.

4. Tasks

The exported methods go in R/toxval-predict.R after the drc method, documented with @describeIn toxval_predict. Their helpers go in R/toxval-predict-bayesnec.R. roxygen takes the \name of a merged topic from the first block it reads, and reads files in C-locale order, in which toxval-predict-bayesnec.R precedes toxval-predict.R. With the methods there, man/toxval_predict.Rd was named toxval_predict.bayesnecfit (found in task 2). An @include would fix the order only by adding a Collate field to DESCRIPTION. Tests go in tests/testthat/test-toxval-predict-bayesnec.R, which calls skip_if_not_installed("bayesnec") at the top. air.toml is present, so R code is formatted with air before each commit. NEWS.md is written by fledge from commit messages and is not edited by hand.

The decision record (task 0)

  • Add T35 to notes/implementation/02_decisions.md after T34, stating §1.1 and §1.4.
  • Amend every toxval passage in §1.2.
  • Draft a decision comment for #39 in notes/drafts/issue-39-toxval-methods-comment.md, following CLAUDE.md §14. #68 holds the decision, its reason and the superseded split, so the comment is the decision in one sentence and a link to #68. RF posts it.
  • Cite #68 in T35.

The refactor documents are also edited on PR #66 (AP, T34; REFACTOR-claude.md in 4b90146). Task 0 is therefore done after #66 merges into phase-2, as the last task before the pull request opens. By then the next free decision number is known, and the passages in §1.2 no longer change under the edit. Edit only the passages listed.

Done when no passage in §1.2 still places the methods in bayesnec, except as history.

Fixtures (task 1)

Add to data-raw/DATASET.R, each saved with compress = "xz" and passed through strip_stanmodel():

fixture fit tests
bayesnec_manec_example bayesnec::manec_example model average, §3.2

The fixtures already total 5.4 MB, against the 5 MB CRAN suggests for a package tarball. manec_example was 1.09 MB as an unstripped xz file. Size is settled when phase 6 prepares the package for CRAN. A fit needed only by tests/local/ can then be kept out of the built package, as bayesnec does with ^tests/local$ in its .Rbuildignore. Record the size of each new fixture in the pull request.

Found in task 2: loaded without bayesnec installed, bayesnec_logx warns that the bayesnec namespace was replaced by .GlobalEnv. The family objects that bayesnec’s validate_family() returns hold a reference to a bayesnec function frame. This was shown for "beta", for Beta(link = "identity") and for binomial, each saved and then loaded in a session with bayesnec removed from the library path. brms::Beta(link = "identity") called directly loads cleanly, as do bnec_model_1 and bayesnec_binomial. The fit is stored as bnec() returned it. The tests that use it are skipped without bayesnec, so the warning is the only effect.

The single-fit method (task 2)

  • toxval_predict.bayesnecfit(), toxval_predict.bnecfit(), check_bayesnec_installed(), bayesnec_available(), bnec_x_var(), bnec_grid(), chk_bayesnec_supported(), as §3.1.
  • build_meta() gains ... (§3.1). The optional elements are added in task 3, where they are first used and tested.
  • bayesnec in Suggests, approved by RF on 2026-10-23.

Tests, on bnec_model_1 (nechorme, beta), bayesnec_nec4param, bayesnec_ecx4param (both gaussian), bayesnec_binomial and bayesnec_logx:

  1. curves[[1]] is identical to bayesnec’s posterior_epred(fit, newdata = bnec_newdata(fit, resolution = r)).
  2. x_vec equals the grid column; a supplied x_range ends the grid and a supplied x_control starts it, and an x_range that starts elsewhere stops (T41).

Tests, on bayesnec_manec_example:

  1. The curve matrix is identical to bayesnec’s posterior_epred(fit, newdata = bnec_newdata(fit, resolution = r)).
  2. table(meta$draw_model) equals round(n * wi) per equation.
  3. meta$model_weights equals mod_stats$wi, named.

Asymptotes and the component anchor (task 4)

Phase 4 added the asymptote slot (T24), type = "relative" and anchor (T23) on PR #66 (2436858).

  • Fill asymptote as §3.4.
  • Make anchor = "component" group the realisations by meta$draw_model, and take each equation’s reference from meta$model_control (§3.2).

Phase 4 records anchor on the result without grouping the realisations (compute_nsec() at 2436858), so the grouping is added here, treating a NULL meta$draw_model as one equation. Until then compute_nsec() refuses "component" when meta$draw_model is present (c3c0dd8), because the pooled reference would otherwise be returned labelled "component".

Tests: on bayesnec_nec4param the decreasing asymptote equals the b_bot_Intercept draws; on bnec_model_1 (nechorme, beta, no bot) it is 0; on a copy with the family set to gaussian it is NA and relative stops; on bayesnec_manec_example the "component" reference of each equation equals the sig_val quantile of that equation’s control over every draw of its fit, and "model" equals the pooled quantile. meta$model_control equals the control column of each equation’s posterior_epred(), and its rows at the index equal the realisations’ controls.

Done when type = "relative" and both anchors are tested on the model set.

5. Branch and dependencies

phase-7-bayesnec-methods was branched from upstream/phase-4-5-spine-and-tibble at 9a3b846, and rebased onto 6bdd99c on 2026-10-23 and onto 2436858 on 2026-10-26. #66 merged into phase-2 on 2026-10-28 with a merge commit, so its commits are ancestors of phase-2 and no --onto rebase is needed.

On 2026-10-29 the branch was rebased onto issue-73-x-control (PR #78, at aa43cda), because #73 changes how every method sets x_control. #78 merged into phase-2 the same day with a merge commit, whose content equals aa43cda. The pull request is opened from beckyfisher:phase-7-bayesnec-methods into open-AIMS:phase-2, ready for review. #77, AP’s documentation review, is merged last. It edits the same comments in R/compute.R, R/toxval-predict.R, test-ecx.R and test-nsec.R, so it is rebased over this branch.

A later rebase onto upstream/phase-2 conflicts mainly in R/toxval-predict.R, where the methods sit beside the brmsfit and drc methods, and in DESCRIPTION, NAMESPACE and man/, which devtools::document() regenerates.

Every task now needs only code that is merged or on PR #66. Task 4 can start, and task 5 waits only for task 4. Phase 6, CRAN publication, is not a prerequisite of any task.

6. Decisions and points for review

RF approved two of these on 2026-10-23: bayesnec in Suggests (§3.1) and fixture size (task 1, §4). RF ruled on 2026-10-29 that under anchor = "component" each equation’s reference is taken over every draw of its fit (§3.2), reversing the acceptance on 2026-10-23 of the difference from using the realisations alone. The rest are listed in BAYESNEC-human.md §6. The arguments are in §3.2 (the draw index), §3.3 (scope), §3.4 (threshold) and §2.1 (the predictor scale).
